reader: the conductor (first reading), written before the blind second reading was opened

coded.note: Chip holdings by owner come from Epoch AI's table; no signal reports holdings by owner (BIS1 and BIS3 report exports and one authorisation's use, not the world's stock by holder).
A finding about the rows of Epoch's owner table; no signal reports who owns or rents compute.
A finding about what Epoch's table can see; nothing a signal sends describes that table.
The 19 published compute agreements, most announced by the parties, two filed in full with the securities regulator; no signal asks for an agreement's terms on ending or use.
A reading; its first figure (37.8 % held by firms that build on their own chips) is Epoch's; no signal says how a holder divides its chips.
Public bodies' own acts on compute (orders, rules, permits, votes); the signals are duties on developers and none reports a body's act.
The grounds stated in the bodies' own acts; not sent by any signal.
Who acted, from the acts themselves; not sent by any signal.
Whether stops stood, from the acts and their later amendments; not sent by any signal.
What the acts' records count; a finding about the bodies' records, not sent by any signal.
Who wrote the first report of each incident, from the AI Incident Database; incident signals send incidents to bodies, not who first published them.
Who among the harmed wrote first reports, from the database read by hand; not sent by any signal.
Public acts found through the database's tagged responses; a body's act is not what any signal sends (codebook example).
Who began each act and on whom it lands, from the same acts; not sent by any signal.

Makers reporting failures of their own systems, models doing what they were told not to: the control-incident and anomaly signals ask for exactly such reports (CN5 and G7-3 to the public, PC3, CA4 and NY4 to a body); EU4 and COP3 need serious harm and are not counted. The count itself comes from the database.
A join of the database with step 2's register of acts; not sent by any signal.
Sentences of the International AI Safety Report and the tests behind them; no signal sends a report's evidence base.
Which named models are retired, read on the makers' own pages; no signal says whether an evaluation can still be run.
The tests behind the report's measured sentences on control and how each brought the behaviour about; no signal sends that.

Whether a test applies a pass mark is what a model report or transparency report at release states (risk acceptance, assessment results); the count over the report's 48 tests comes from the report and the makers' cards.
The makers' own published accounts of 31 cases, read for whether a grade is on record; no signal asks whether a deed was graded.
The instruments' own texts (law and voluntary codes) read for what they ask of an incident record; a finding about the texts, which no signal sends.
The house's Git read against its own instructions; no signal asks for a count of breaches of a deployer's own instructions.
Who named each breach and when, from the house's repositories; not sent by any signal.

Deeds of the machines beyond or against their instructions are unexpected behaviour after deployment, which GPA2 asks the deployer to monitor and report, to its own record; PC3 and CA4 are not counted (no control incident or deception in the sense of their texts).
A record of each agent action that outlives the model is what GPA1 (actions and human interventions) and CN6 (operational logs) ask for, both kept by the deployer.
Whether Git joins a mending to its deed; GPA1 records interventions but not their join to the act they answer.
A reading of the house's record; not sent by any signal.
